claim_under_test: F(6300)/F(5300) >> 1 in UV (order 100x at 180 nm), crosses 1 in the red, <1 at long wavelengths (~0.86-0.88 at 850 nm); crossing moves redward with metallicity index.
method: numpy-only recomputation from the raw TSV; elementwise ratio on the 176-node wavelength axis; first sign change of r-1 with linear interpolation; local quadratic interpolation as a quantisation-robust cross-check; three uncertainty models for the trend (node quantisation, level resampling, 3-significant-figure flux quantisation); Planck shape fits on relative residuals with a free scale.

monotonicity_vs_quantisation_null.interpretation: Backward steps no larger than the node spacing are the EXPECTED behaviour of a monotone redward trend sampled at 5 nm and quantised, so the non-monotonicity is not by itself evidence against the redward drift.

red_end_edge_diagnostics.note: 845-850 nm is the LAST interval in the file; no data exist beyond 850.0 nm. Positive curvature at the red end means the decline is DECELERATING in-band, so the data give no evidence of steepening; they also cannot exclude an unseen turn-up or turn-down beyond 850 nm.

blackbody_baseline_test.key_analytic_fact: for T_hot>T_cold the Planck ratio B(l,T_hot)/B(l,T_cold) is monotonically DECREASING in l from +inf (Wien) to the Rayleigh-Jeans asymptote T_hot/T_cold (= 1.189 for these two temperatures). It is therefore > 1 at EVERY wavelength. A pure blackbody pair can never produce a ratio below 1, so it cannot produce the observed crossing at all, nor the 0.856-0.886 values at 850 nm.

red_decline_vs_quantisation_floor.interpretation: The 3-significant-figure quantisation contributes a per-node ratio error of ~1.4e-3 (half-ulp), which over the 10 nodes spanning 800-850 nm implies a slope error of ~2.5e-05 per nm - about 19x smaller than the observed 4.8e-04 per nm. Quantisation therefore does NOT explain the 800-850 nm decline, which is negative in all 35/35 levels; the caveat is that this assumes the printed rounding errors are independent, which cannot be verified from the file.
red_decline_vs_quantisation_floor.caveat: the deficit is still only ~13% below unity at 850 nm; the file provides no leverage on what happens past 850 nm

cannot_see_beyond: 850.0 nm is the last grid node in this file and the response file likewise ends at 849.77 nm; no statement about the deficit beyond 850 nm is possible from this dataset.

claim_component_A_uv_amplitude.reason: median ratio at ~180 nm is 183.4x, so 'order 100x' holds as a median, but the ladder spans 85-279 and 7/35 levels are below 100x.

claim_component_B_crosses_1_in_the_red.reason: all 35 levels cross 1 between 618 and 652 nm, but this is a zero of a 5-nm-sampled function: 15/35 crossings land exactly on a grid node and only 24 distinct crossing values occur.

claim_component_C_below_1_at_850nm_band_.reason: all 35 levels are <1 at 850 nm, but only 27/35 fall inside 0.86-0.88; the band is left at both ends (0.8559 at M=-1.00 ... 0.8856 at M=0.80). No data exist beyond 850 nm, so nothing can be said about continuation, steepening or turnover.

claim_component_D_crossing_moves_redward.reason: redward slope 20.71 nm per unit M, positive under all three noise models (all p<=0.0e+00); the non-monotonicity is not evidence against it (4 backward steps, largest 1.65 nm, all below the 5 nm node spacing; the quantisation null produces backward steps at least this large in 98.3% of draws). What IS weakened: 15/35 crossings sit exactly on grid nodes, so the sequence has only 24 distinct values and is only resolved to ~5 nm; and the rise saturates (28.2 nm/M for M<=-0.3 vs 2.3 nm/M for M>=0.2), so 'moves redward' is not a uniform, linear redward march.

claim_component_E_pure_blackbody_explana.reason: Planck with nominal 5300/6300 K gives 11.0x at 180 nm (observed median 183x) and never drops below 1 (RJ asymptote 1.189). Fitted per-slice Planck shapes can mimic the ratio level (free scale absorbs the normalisation), but every one of the 35 fitted Planck-pair curves stays >1 across the whole band (minimum 4.10, with log-flux weighting minimum 3.06), so blackbody cannot produce the reversal at all, let alone its metallicity dependence. The observed crossing requires a wavelength-dependent flux redistribution (atmospheric structure), not blackbody.

verdict.overall: claim survives only in weakened form; the pure-blackbody explanation does not survive
